usage: Used to describe something with little or no moisture, especially in everyday gardening and plant-care contexts.
Very common before nouns, e.g. describing soil, leaves, weather, or stored plant material; it sounds natural and simple.
Can also be used after verbs or in short descriptive phrases to say something has become dry; learners often hear it in speaking more than formal writing.
In plant care, this word is useful when checking whether soil, stems, or leaves need water; it is a basic, high-frequency word.
